clue.text: Minor celebrity coterie popping ecstasy, becoming very hot

indicators.note: the minor-celebrity group pops (swallows) a pill, so the drug's letter goes inside

parts.note: B-list is the second tier of fame, the minor celebrities
a ring is a close clique or coterie
E is the standard abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A clique of second-rate celebrities takes ecstasy and overheats at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'popping' looks like a party verb but signals insertion: the group pops (swallows) the E. B-list is the second tier of fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Blistering heat is heat fierce enough to raise blisters, an intensifying adjective for extreme temperature.

clue.text: Crustacea clean when cooked in pubs

indicators.note: the cooked letters are placed inside the word for pubs

parts.note: bars are pubs

indicators.note: cooking changes the form of something, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shellfish are cleaned and then cooked in pub kitchens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cooked' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion; the kitchen picture hides both.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnacles are sessile marine arthropods belonging to the crustacean group, so they are examples of crustaceans.

clue.text: 30 or 21 say, for instance put in ground outside

indicators.note: the word for burying goes round the outside of the abbreviation

parts.note: to inter is to bury, put in the ground

explanation.surface: Something buried in the ground is offered as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: '30' and '21' look like cross-references to other clues, but here they are just whole numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirty and twenty-one are whole numbers, and a whole number is what mathematicians call this.

clue.text: Bit of training by hospital to take pulse

indicators.note: a bit of the word training is just its opening letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
to rob is to take unlawfully

explanation.surface: A medical trainee at the hospital learns how to take a patient's pulse.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular beat, like the beat of the heart felt in the wrist.

clue.text: Go over in box cart?

parts.note: re means 'in the matter of', so it stands for 'in'
a hearse is a vehicle that carries a box, the coffin

explanation.surface: A question about checking something stored in a box on a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' is slang for a coffin, so a cart for a box is a funeral vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To go over a speech or a play is to practise it before the real performance.

clue.text: Pest is abandoned in shade

indicators.note: the two letters of the word is are given up, dropped from the pest

parts.note: a nuisance is a pest
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pest has been left behind in the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' drops IS from NUISANCE. 'shade' looks like shadow, but it means a subtle difference here.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade of meaning or colour is a fine distinction, a subtle gradation.

clue.text: What 21 did in radio report is sad

indicators.note: a radio report is heard, not read, so the word is a sound-alike

parts.note: 21 across is typhoons, and what such storms did is blew

explanation.surface: A sad radio report about what happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 across is TYPHOONS; typhoons blew, and BLEW is said the same as the colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue is a common idiom for feeling low or melancholy.

clue.text: Uncovered blue and silver inlaid Fabergé creation turning up in cases

indicators.note: the word blue loses its outer letters, its covering
silver is set into the reversed egg like an inlay
in a down clue, turning up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: Fabergé is famous for jewelled eggs
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A blue-and-silver Fabergé egg is unwrapped from its packing cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' strips the outer letters, 'turning up' reverses (this is a down clue) and 'inlaid' sets the silver in.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage means a traveller's bags and suitcases taken together.

clue.text: Had breakfast — would be defeated after slice of bacon

indicators.note: the answer would only become the longer word if a letter were added
the answer follows the letter from bacon, so taking that letter away leaves it

parts.note: beaten means defeated

indicators.note: a slice of bacon is just its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone who has eaten breakfast feels beaten after a slice of bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: put B (a slice of bacon) in front of the answer and you would get BEATEN, defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one has had as a meal has been consumed; the past participle fits 'having had breakfast'.

clue.text: Sloppy make-up's run

parts.note: slap is British slang for make-up
to dash is to run

explanation.surface: Messy make-up has run.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link word meaning 'has'. SLAP is informal British for cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is careless and hasty, done in a sloppy way.

clue.text: What goes around comes around, all the same

definitions.text: What goes around comes around, all the same

indicators.note: the word reads the same coming back around from the other end

parts.note: a spinning part of a machine is something that goes around

explanation.surface: The proverb about karma, that what goes around comes around.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole word is a palindrome: read backwards it is all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the spinning part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades, which turns around.

clue.text: It shows the way for lad oddly restricted in stature

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are confined inside the word for stature

parts.note: height is stature

indicators.note: the letters of lad are arranged oddly, in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A short lad leads the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like a call for alternate letters, but here it signals an anagram; 'restricted in' is the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's front lamp lights the road ahead, showing the driver the route.

clue.text: Branch of maths involving a bit of geometry — area, length and breadth

indicators.note: involving here means intricately mixing, so these letters are tangled together
a bit of geometry is just its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Maths that uses a little geometry: area, length and breadth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' mixes G, AREA, L and B into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the branch of mathematics that uses letters and symbols to stand for unknown numbers.

clue.text: Officer liable to be kidnapped by a murderer

indicators.note: the word for liable is captured and held inside the murderer

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
apt means liable, as in 'apt to fail'

explanation.surface: An officer runs the risk of being kidnapped by a killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is a commissioned rank in the army and navy, so an officer.

clue.text: No terms for 'in Rice style'? It's how he might be represented

definitions.text: No terms for 'in Rice style'? It's how he might be represented

indicators.note: the trimmed letters are presented again in a new order
each of the three words loses its final letter, its terminus

parts.note: the three words in, Rice and style are the fodder

explanation.surface: Asking how Tim Rice, the man who wrote words for Lloyd Webber, might be described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No terms for' cuts the last letters off IN, RICE and STYLE to leave IRICSTYL, and 'represented' rearranges those. Tim Rice wrote the words for Evita and Jesus Christ Superstar.
explanation.definitionFit: Tim Rice writes the words for musicals, so the job title for a writer of song words describes him.

clue.text: Caught on battlefield, in the soup

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written
the Somme was a major battlefield of the First World War

explanation.surface: Someone caught on a battlefield is in serious trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' is a British idiom for being in trouble, but 'soup' alone is the definition. The Somme is a river in France where a huge 1916 battle was fought.
explanation.definitionFit: Consommé is a clear broth made from concentrated stock, a type of soup.

clue.text: A picture maker arrived with another?

parts.note: came means arrived
another picture maker is an RA, a Royal Academician, an artist elected to the Royal Academy

explanation.surface: A photographer turns up with a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another picture maker: an RA is a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera makes photographs, so it is a device that makes pictures.

clue.text: Making appointment as nitwit mixed double gin

parts.note: an ass is a fool, a nitwit

indicators.note: the doubled spirit is mixed like a cocktail, its letters rearranged
the word gin is taken twice, a double measure

explanation.surface: A fool, drinking a mixed double gin, makes a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' takes the spirit twice and 'mixed' shuffles the six letters; 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Assigning someone to a post means appointing them to it.

clue.text: 'Round cut' — unusual name for a plant

indicators.note: the word for a round is cut short, its tail letter removed

parts.note: a cycle is a round, as in a round of events

indicators.note: the letters of name are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A gardener gives an odd name to a plant after cutting it round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims CYCLE to CYCL, and 'unusual' rearranges NAME to AMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclamen is a flowering plant of the primrose family, often grown as a winter pot plant.

clue.text: A way to hold one in five in a disapproving look

indicators.note: the abbreviation for a way holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born at once

explanation.surface: How a disapproving face might narrow its eyes at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A squint is a narrowing of the eyes, which can show suspicion or disapproval.

clue.text: Refreshed by fruit-filled baked pud

indicators.note: the shuffled pudding is filled with the fruit inside it
baking changes the pudding, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a date is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone is revived by a pudding baked with fruit inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baked' signals the anagram and 'filled' says the fruit goes inside the shuffled pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A refreshed web page or record has been brought up to date.

clue.text: Tea company above and below equator — they make big impact in tropics

definitions.text: they make big impact in tropics

parts.note: Typhoo is a long-established British tea brand
north and south of the equator, abbreviated N and S

explanation.surface: A tea company with plantations either side of the equator.
explanation.walkthrough: TYPHOO is a British brand of tea bags.
explanation.definitionFit: Typhoons are tropical cyclones of the western Pacific that do huge damage when they strike land.

clue.text: Imagine getting up with other ranks and no small space at top in craft

indicators.note: in a down clue the abbreviation for other ranks sits at the top

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: no means the small space is left out
in a down clue, getting up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: an en is a small space in printing, half an em

explanation.surface: Imagine a soldier rising through the ranks at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns IMAGINE into ENIGAMI; 'no' drops EN to leave IGAMI, under OR 'at top'.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into shapes, a handicraft.

clue.text: Drawing of small boat

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A picture of a little boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough drawing done quickly in pencil is a sketch, as is a short comic scene.

clue.text: Got to pop by the pier for some fish

parts.note: had means got, as in 'had a letter'
to dock is to bring a boat alongside the pier

explanation.surface: Someone had to call in by the pier to buy fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pop by the pier' is a playful definition of the verb DOCK; the setter said so on the blog.
explanation.definitionFit: Haddock is a North Atlantic white fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Frequent hotel with relative

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: Someone often visits a hotel with a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frequent' is the verb here, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To frequent a place is to visit it habitually, which is what a regular does at a favourite pub.

clue.text: Tilt and roll

definitions.meaning: a ship leaning to one side, a heel or tilt
a roll is a register of names, an entry in a catalogue

explanation.definitionFit: A ship that leans over is said to list, and a register or catalogue entry is also called this.

clue.text: Ray's succeeded with Katherine

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees
Kate is a short form of Katherine

explanation.surface: A man called Ray has been successful with a woman called Katherine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name but is the fish; 's is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A skate is a flat cartilaginous fish of the ray family.

clue.text: After mid-July lad joins a corporation for final say

indicators.note: the lad comes after the middle of the month
mid means just the central letters of the word July

parts.note: Tim is a boy's name, a lad
corporation is old slang for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: After mid-July a lad joins a company and gets the last word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' means a large belly in old British slang, and TUM is a tummy.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultimatum is a final demand, with threats if it is refused.

clue.text: Graduate about to invest in artificial intelligence calculators

indicators.note: the graduate and about are placed inside the abbreviation, like money invested

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
c, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A graduate is about to invest in artificial intelligence and its counting machines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like 'going to', but 'about' gives C and 'to invest in' is the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the plural of abacus, the bead frame used for counting.

clue.text: Off and on, this day is fairly good

indicators.note: taking letters on and leaving them off by turns picks alternate letters

explanation.surface: Someone's verdict on today's weather, which has been patchy but fairly good.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidy sum is a fairly large amount, so the word can mean considerable or fairly good.

clue.text: Tremendous falling short in course of affair

indicators.note: the word for falling short goes into the middle of the affair

parts.note: a thing is an affair, as in 'having a thing'
under means below a target, falling short

explanation.surface: Someone falls short during a love affair, which is tremendous.
explanation.definitionFit: Thundering is an informal intensifier, as in a thundering great mistake, meaning huge.
